newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ASHANTI, GOLD DEPRESS ZIMBABWE MINE INDEX.
newsitem.headline: ASHANTI, GOLD DEPRESS ZIMBABWE MINE INDEX.

text.p: The Zimbabwe Stock Exchange's mining index has fallen to a 29-month low, depressed by weakness in Ghana's Ashanti Goldfields Ltd which itself has been pressured by a weak gold price, analysts said on Thursday.
Ashanti Goldfields, a gold mining and exploration company, dominates the seven stock index with a weighting of more than two thirds.
No recovery was seen soon unless the gold price bounced and buoyed Ashanti shares, the analysts said.

"The index has to a large extent suffered due to Ashanti and the decline in the gold price. In the near future, unless the gold price recovers to $355-60 an ounce, there's little to be expected from minings," said an analyst who asked not to be identified.
The Zimbabwe Stock Exchange's (ZSE) mining shares fell 41.28 points on Wednesday to finish at 968.59 -- its lowest since September 8, 1994 when it closed at 957.85.
"Since 1994 we have not seen levels as low as it is now," Dataworld investment analyst Jason Moore told Reuters.

Analysts said that with only seven companies, the mining index was extremely volatile and sensitive to any commodity price fluctuations like the recent slide in the gold price which hit fresh three year lows last week.
"The mining sector on the ZSE is very small and gold makes up the bulk of the counters quoted," Moore said.
Ashanti is estimated to have a market capitalisation of Z$8.5 billion of the mining index's total Z$11 billion.
Other gold companies listed are Falcon, Falgold and Rio Tinto . The remaining mining companies are Bindura Nickel , MCM and Wankie.

"Ashanti has a very large market cap. If Ashanti goes up strongly, the whole mining index goes up. If Ashanti goes down, the whole index goes down. Ashanti has a huge influence on the index," an analyst said.
Ashanti was untraded on Wednesday but has lost five percent since the start of 1997 and was last bid at Z$90.00.
"Traditionally the mining index has been very volatile. Ashanti has probably lessened the volatility but now the index is dependent on what Ashanti is going to do," Moore said.
Analysts said that mining shares could reach levels at which they were good value for money and then enjoy some buying but that this would still depend on the bullion price.
"There has to be some value in these low levels but no short-term bounce is expected in these companies unless the gold price climbs," Moore said.

Turning to the base-metal stocks, analysts said that commodity prices in general had been depressed last year and that this, combined with production problems at a number of Zimbabwe companies, had knocked these stocks.
"There has been a trend of production problems throughout the mining sector in Zimbabwe," Moore said.
